html:
SMTO-EML-0023 — Your email sender's security certificate can't be loaded

GUID: a1ebfcfc-106b-5ab1-94d7-62c5fd9c4003
Slug: email-custom-ca-invalid
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • This sender is set to check the mail server with a certificate you supplied, but that certificate is missing or damaged. SMTO stopped before connecting, so nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask your mail administrator for the mail server's certificate authority (CA) certificate. It is text that starts with -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----. SMTO needs that exact certificate to confirm it is talking to your real mail server.
  2. Open More options › Parameter Store, select the sender, open Value, select Reveal & edit value, paste the whole certificate into ca_pem, then select Save. The ca_pem entry is empty or holds text that isn't a usable certificate.
  3. If your mail server uses a normal public certificate, change verification from custom_ca to system instead, and select Save. SMTO then uses the computer's built-in trusted certificates, so no custom one is needed.
  4. Ask SMTO in a conversation to test the connection for this sender. The test confirms SMTO can now check the server's identity.

What success looks like

  • The connection test succeeds and reports a verified secure connection.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to your mail administrator or the person who manages SMTO. Don't set verification to insecure to get past this; that turns off the check that protects your password.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Building the SMTP TLS context failed: tls.verification is custom_ca but tls.ca_pem is empty or ssl load_verify_locations rejected it.

What this means

  • The selected custom CA configuration is missing or cannot be loaded. The producer identifies the failed field or preparation stage without exposing private values.

Why this can happen

  • Custom CA data is absent or the TLS library cannot load it.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the reported field, failure phase and retained receipt before choosing a correction.

How to fix it

  • Inspect tls.verification and tls.ca_pem in the email_smtp Parameter Store record. Supply a valid PEM CA certificate that ssl load_verify_locations(cadata=...) accepts, or set verification to system for publicly trusted servers, then run email.test_connection; do not switch to insecure.
  • Correct the custom CA PEM in the saved TLS configuration, then test the connection with certificate verification enabled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first. Retry only when existing execution and effect evidence permits it; reconcile an uncertain prior send.

How to verify the fix

  • The custom CA loads and the connection verifies the server certificate.

What not to do

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.

Technical notes

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
